prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
Bards do not simply cast their abilities — they compose songs from
  components slotted into a song book. 80 components are recorded.
prose_evidence.source_html: Bards do not simply cast their abilities — they compose songs from components slotted into a song book. 80 components are recorded.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
Depending on level, a bard has between one and seven component types available: Melody, Embellishment, Lyric, Chorus, Verse,
      Bridge and Coda. Each type offers one to three slots for a single
      component. By level 50 a bard can mix and match up to sixteen separate
      components in one song.
prose_evidence.source_html: Depending on level, a bard has between one and seven component types available: Melody, Embellishment, Lyric, Chorus, Verse, Bridge and Coda. Each type offers one to three slots for a single component. By level 50 a bard can mix and match up to sixteen separate components in one song.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
Components pulse once every four seconds. Many are persistent and hold
      their effect for the whole song — Harmony of War adds its damage
      continuously, with no pulse. Others, such as the regeneration songs,
      only deliver their benefit on each four-second tick.
prose_evidence.source_html: Components pulse once every four seconds. Many are persistent and hold their effect for the whole song — Harmony of War adds its damage continuously, with no pulse. Others, such as the regeneration songs, only deliver their benefit on each four-second tick.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
Every component charges its energy cost each second the
      song plays. A bard offsets this two ways. The first is natural energy
      regeneration, which scales with Vitality and ticks every second just as
      the cost does.
prose_evidence.source_html: Every component charges its energy cost each second the song plays. A bard offsets this two ways. The first is natural energy regeneration, which scales with Vitality and ticks every second just as the cost does.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
The second is rests . A rest occupies a slot but subtracts from the song's running cost rather than adding to it,
      so an 8-point rest makes a 20-cost song cost 12. A rest may go in any
      component row except a Melody, and only one may be used per song.
prose_evidence.source_html: The second is rests. A rest occupies a slot but subtracts from the song's running cost rather than adding to it, so an 8-point rest makes a 20-cost song cost 12. A rest may go in any component row except a Melody, and only one may be used per song.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
Status records whether a component functions on the VGO
  emulator, not whether it worked in the live game: Working , Partial , or Unscripted (present but with no effect
  implemented). Single use marks a component that can only be
  slotted once, where most may be stacked.
prose_evidence.source_html: Status records whether a component functions on the VGO emulator, not whether it worked in the live game: Working, Partial, or Unscripted (present but with no effect implemented). Single use marks a component that can only be slotted once, where most may be stacked.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
Rests reduce a song's total cost by their value, shown here as a negative
      number. They may be slotted into any row except a Melody, one per song.
prose_evidence.source_html: Rests reduce a song's total cost by their value, shown here as a negative number. They may be slotted into any row except a Melody, one per song.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed:
Recorded discrepancy: the guide text describes seven rests worth 2, 4, 5, 7,
  8, 10 and 12, plus an eighth worth 11 obtained from a mob drop at level 50.
  The component table lists seven rests, and the 4-point rest is not among
  them. Both are reproduced as found rather than reconciled.
